_README: PERSONALITY SET for the chain-capable copro core. The MANIFEST is the deliverable;
an .rbf is generated on demand from the recipe below, because building one is a FULL
clean Quartus compile (~40-70 min), not a hex patch.
★ WHY NOT A HEX PATCH: the firmware ROM is loaded with `initial $readmemh(
'copro_rom.hex', rom)` (CoproDrMario.sv:160), which Quartus resolves at SYNTHESIS.
`quartus_cdb --update_mif` therefore has nothing to update, EXITS 0, and quartus_asm
re-emits an IDENTICAL bitstream. Measured: three 'different' arms all produced rbf
f7d3382a. See swap_arm.sh, which is disabled and kept as the record. The RTL comment
in CoproDrMario.sv claiming arm-switching is 'a firmware hex patch -- NOT a two-hour
resynthesis' is ASPIRATIONAL AND REFUTED; it is flagged for correction.
★ THE ACCEPTANCE GATE EXISTS BECAUSE THAT FAILURE IS SILENT AND DANGEROUS: a core
built from the wrong firmware still PLAYS WELL (arm registers power up to 0 = lnk1, a
real 60.2% brain), so it looks fine while being mislabelled. Every build must assert
the new rbf md5 DIFFERS from every other personality's. A flag existing is not a flag

arm_registers.note: Written by the copro FIRMWARE to its OWN bus ($70E5/$70E6 are decoded off AB, the coprocessor's internal 6502 bus). NOT cart-writable: the cart only drives prg_ain ($5000-$51FF). A cart-side write, or readback, would be on the wrong bus entirely.
arm_registers.$70E5: a_fix  -- 0 = one clear round (lnk1 physics), 1 = resolve to fixpoint
arm_registers.$70E6: a_chw  -- DRCHAIN dose / 4 (0 = no chain reward)
arm_registers.powerup: both 0, so firmware writing neither behaves as lnk1 / no-chain

gate.firmware_identity: the built core's copro_rom.hex md5 MUST equal this entry's firmware.md5
gate.distinctness: the built rbf md5 MUST differ from every other personality's rbf md5
gate.fit_verdict: fresh placement each time -- worst setup slack must clear +0.10 on the pinned seed; if it misses, HOLD that personality and report rather than seed-hunting

personalities.honest_line: 60.2% [56.9, 63.4] vs the shipped winner, holdout-CONFIRMED and stronger on holdout than on tune. Wins by OUT-RACING, not attacking: ~99% of its wins are clear-first and garbage decides 5 matches in 800. Garbage-off it still scores 55.1%, so the edge is mostly a genuine SOLO speed edge.

70.9% at L11 / 76.5% at L17 vs the shipped winner. The edge is GARBAGE-MEDIATED: paired ON-minus-OFF is +16.8 [+11.7, +21.8], and without the attack channel it falls to 54.0%. It also never dies -- 400 losses across both levels contain ZERO topouts and ZERO stalls; it loses only by being cleared first.

★ A STYLE CHOICE, NOT A STRICT UPGRADE. 75.4% with garbage ON but 52.8% with it OFF, and that OFF confidence interval CONTAINS 50% -- i.e. NO MEASURABLE SOLO EDGE. Its whole win is the attack channel. Bigger chains to watch; do not read 'spicy' as 'stronger'.

Fixpoint cascade resolution with NO chain reward -- the control that separates 'resolving cascades properly' from 'being rewarded for building them'. Included so the Stomper's edge can be attributed rather than assumed. Not tuned as a play arm.
